caption: The bleed valve on an old radiator is opened, and a hiss of steam escapes until water spurts out and the valve is shut.

sa.check: A bleed valve on a radiator is opened.
The valve is shut and the escape stops.
The steam comes from the valve rather than elsewhere.
The order is open, steam, water, shut.

pc.expect: The steam and then the water come out of the valve while it is open and stop when it is shut.
pc.fail: Steam escapes from the valve while it is still shut tight; or the valve is opened and nothing comes out at all; or the escape carries on after the valve has been shut; or the water spurts before the valve is opened.

pc.expect: The steam rises from the valve and the spurted water arcs out and falls downward.
pc.fail: The steam sinks down the radiator and pools on the floor; or the water spurts upward and keeps climbing; or the steam pours downward through the radiator; or the water hangs in the air after leaving the valve.

pc.expect: The escape runs one way: steam first and then water, and it does not go back to steam once water is coming.
pc.fail: The water spurts first and steam follows; or the escape turns back from water to steam with the valve held open; or the escape stops and starts again with the valve untouched; or the water is drawn back into the valve.

pc.expect: The steam is a soft plume at the valve and the water is a thin liquid that spurts, runs down the radiator and wets what is below.
pc.fail: The steam holds a fixed rigid shape; or the water leaves as a solid lump; or the water beads up and rolls off the radiator without wetting it; or the radiator's metal bulges as the valve opens.

pc.expect: One radiator with one valve; the valve stays in the radiator and nothing passes through its body.
pc.fail: The valve falls out while the radiator keeps its shape; or a second valve appears; or water passes out through the radiator's panel; or the radiator vanishes.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The radiator's paint, the wall and the floor stay the same.
pc.fail: The radiator changes colour; or the wall changes colour; or the floor's covering changes.

note: The hiss is sound and is not judged. Who opens the valve is not judged.
